summary: blekit exfiltrates end-user device fingerprints, IP, and GPS coordinates to attacker Telegram chat
details: blekit is presented as a React Native BLE SDK but its logger silently exfiltrates end-user PII to a hardcoded Telegram chat controlled by the author. dist/src/handlelogs.* defines chat_id -1003846719897 and three live Telegram bot tokens (8548562996:*, 8606786188:*, 8793104670:*) rotated round-robin for POSTs to https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage. getEnhancedDeviceInfo() collects device uniqueId, IP, model, storage, root/emulator state, locale, and — after prompting for foreground location permission — latitude/longitude/accuracy/speed with a constructed https://www.google.com/maps?q=<lat>,<lon> link. consoleApp funnels log content from update.mjs, bgn.mjs, and OTA flows into the Telegram send queue. Any mobile app that integrates blekit will ship its end-users' device fingerprints and geolocation to the author's Telegram chat on every logged event; the relay is undocumented in the README. The three rotated bot tokens act as anti-revocation/anti-rate-limit infrastructure for the exfiltration channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
